PullRequest.Title: voice: categorize invalid confirmation narration drops
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- add a bounded `rejectionReason` category to `voiceNarrationDropped` for invalid confirmation narrations
- allowlist `stale_pending` and map absent or unrecognized backend values to `missing` or `unknown`
- preserve existing accepted, busy, suppressed, retry, and non-confirmation behavior
- add focused regression coverage for known, missing, unknown, accepted, and busy acknowledgements

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceClient/voiceSessionController.test.ts --grep 'busy, invalid, and legacy suppressed checkpoints|categorizes invalid confirmation narration'`\n\nFixes #336607

Scenarios.Scenario: Backend rejects a solicited confirmation narration as invalid while voice mode is active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A WebSocket narration_ack is parsed and synchronously emitted to VoiceSessionController._handleNarrationAck; pending state is cleared and the already-existing voiceNarrationDropped telemetry call runs. The new reason mapping is a constant-time string comparison on this path. Telemetry transport is not awaited, so it is not on the voice interaction's blocking network critical path, although local cleaning/appender dispatch executes synchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one request_narration over the existing WebSocket and receive/parse its acknowledgement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one acknowledgement per sent narration request; _narrate suppresses duplicate in-flight requests for the same session/kind/identity, and the diff does not change request cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request and acknowledgement crossed the WebSocket and were parsed/emitted before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The acknowledgement must be handled to clear the pending narration state, but the WebSocket operation and JSON parsing already existed unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the existing voiceNarrationDropped event to the telemetry appender; desktop configurations may forward it over IPC and subsequently batch/send it over the network.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing telemetry event for each invalid or suppressed solicited narration; the new field is included only for invalid confirmations and has one of three constant-size values. No additional event or boundary call is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same voiceNarrationDropped event and telemetry boundary call occurred, with kind and disposition but without the additional bounded rejectionReason property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local event cleaning and appender dispatch are synchronous, but IPC/network completion is not awaited by acknowledgement handling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of solicited confirmation narration requests that receive an invalid acknowledgement. Work remains O(1) per acknowledgement and the event count is unchanged; in-flight duplicate narration requests are deduplicated by session, kind, and narratable identity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: WebSocket messages and controller listeners execute serially on the event loop. Telemetry appender transport is asynchronous; the diff adds no task, promise, queue, retry, or parallel request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced. Existing narration maps deduplicate in-flight requests and remove the acknowledged entry; telemetry may buffer up to its existing fixed limit while experiment properties initialize. Cold and warm behavior differ only in the pre-existing telemetry appender initialization/buffering, not because of the new field.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the complete changed hunk, WebSocket event source, controller call path, narration deduplication, and telemetry service/appender path were traced. The only production work introduced is an O(1) comparison and a constant-sized property on an event already emitted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact invalid-confirmation frequency and telemetry appender configuration vary by user and platform, but payload growth is statically bounded to one short enum string and does not alter call count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change neither adds an expensive boundary nor increases boundary cardinality; its bounded allocation/serialization increment is immaterial and does not scale with backend reason length.

Scenarios.Scenario: Running the focused VoiceSessionController acknowledgement regression test
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test synchronously maps six fixed cases, creating a controller and invoking _narrate and _handleNarrationAck for each before asserting captured in-memory events.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed array of six cases; there is no data-dependent or production-input growth.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely sequential and synchronous under the test's fake timers; no Promise.all, worker, subprocess, or remote concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior is exercised beyond per-controller in-memory narration maps, each used for one request and disposed by the suite store.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete added test and the TestTelemetryService/createController implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the case count is fixed in source and test doubles replace WebSocket, audio, and telemetry transports.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The additional fixed test setup affects only test runtime and performs no filesystem, subprocess, IPC, database, or network operations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Loading the voice controller and telemetry module before handling narration events
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing voiceTelemetry module is imported by VoiceSessionController; this diff adds one type alias and a small function declaration in that already-loaded module.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One function declaration per module evaluation, independent of sessions, narrations, or workspace size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous module evaluation with no added asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Standard module caching means evaluation remains once per renderer/module realm; the diff adds no independent module import or cache entry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the unchanged import source and complete telemetry diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No meaningful magnitude uncertainty: the added executable module work is a single small function definition.
Scenarios.Verdict: No startup or eager-work finding; the module was already required and the added declaration is constant and trivial.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all three changed files. Traced the invalid-confirmation acknowledgement from the existing WebSocket request/ack through narration deduplication and the existing telemetry IPC/network path, plus test-only and module-load behavior. The PR adds only constant-time categorization and one bounded enum property to an event already emitted, with unchanged event/boundary cardinality, no new retention, and no concurrency change. No findings or regression-fix learning signal were warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
